export function buildQueue(
  candidates: QueueCandidate[],
  today: BusinessDate,
  config: QueueConfig,
  /**
   * The instant, for the same-day retry alone. Everything else here works in
   * business dates; an hour-later retry is the one rule that cannot.
   */
  nowMs: number = Date.parse(`${today}T23:59:59+05:30`),
): QueueResult {
  const weights = config["queue.tierWeights"];
  const entries: QueueEntry[] = [];
  const suppressed: SuppressedEntry[] = [];

  for (const c of candidates) {
    const all = reasonsFor(c, today, config, weights, nowMs);
    if (!all.length) continue;

    /*
     * A customer nobody can reach is ONE thing, not a list of things.
     *
     * The ladder is spent, so asking for an order is not the work — deciding
     * what happens to them is: a different number, a different time of day, a
     * visit, or leaving them alone. Presenting them as an ordinary order call
     * beside that would invite a sixth unanswered ring.
     */
    const unreachable = all.find((r) => r.kind === "unreachable");
    if (unreachable) {
      entries.push({
        customerId: c.customerId,
        name: c.name,
        score: unreachable.weight,
        reasons: [unreachable],
        outstanding: c.outstanding,
        callValue: callValuePaise(unreachable.kind, c),
        targetGap: c.targetGap,
        daysSinceContact: c.lastContactDate
          ? daysBetween(c.lastContactDate, today)
          : null,
      });
      continue;
    }

    // A reminder is a promise the telecaller made. It overrides the quiet
    // window and the no-order cooldown, but not do-not-contact.
    const hasReminderReason = all.some(
      (r) => r.kind === "reminderOverdue" || r.kind === "reminderDueToday",
    );

    // The quiet window silences ORDER CHASING, not the customer. Order reasons
    // are stripped rather than the whole customer suppressed, so a telecaller
    // with a reminder or a check-in against them still sees the call they are
    // actually making rather than one about an order.
    //
    // `orderStatus` is stripped here too, though it does not ask for another
    // order the way the other three do — it still names THIS order, taken
    // inside the window, and nothing about its approval status changes in the
    // day or two right after it was placed. Without this a customer who
    // ordered this morning came back tomorrow asking to be told "still
    // waiting for accounts", which is the quiet window's own fact read back to
    // them as a reason to call. Once the window ends the order may well still
    // be unresolved and worth a real check-in — this only holds it back for as
    // long as the order is fresh. See `isOrderChasing`.
    const quiet = quietWindow(c, today, config, hasReminderReason);

    // A held reminder is a wider, deliberate version of the same idea: not
    // "the order was just placed" but "a telecaller decided this promise
    // covers it, hold everything order/cycle-shaped until then." Money and
    // do-not-contact are never in the stripped set — see `isHoldableReason`.
    const hold = holdWindow(c, today);

    // A lead the field team is climbing a ladder with is not a prospect for
    // the office to cold-call — and, since Mahek's own rule, not a reorder for
    // it to chase either. See `funnelHold`.
    const funnel = funnelHold(c);

    // What the customer said last time somebody asked. It silences the ASK
    // and nothing else — see `outcomeWindow`, which used to suppress the whole
    // customer and so answered a question about an order by cancelling a
    // promise, a debt and a check-in along with it.
    const outcome = outcomeWindow(c, today, config, hasReminderReason);

    let reasons = quiet ? all.filter((r) => !isOrderChasing(r.kind)) : all;
    if (hold) reasons = reasons.filter((r) => !isHoldableReason(r.kind));
    if (funnel) {
      reasons = reasons.filter((r) => r.kind !== "prospect" && !isReorderChasing(r.kind));
    }
    if (outcome) reasons = reasons.filter((r) => !isOrderAsk(r.kind));

    // Suppression is a return value, not a filter. The interface has a strip
    // that explains who is missing and why; silently dropping them would
    // remove a telecaller's ability to understand their own queue.
    //
    // Read BEFORE the emptied-by-a-window sentence below, and that ordering is
    // load-bearing. These are facts about the WHOLE CUSTOMER — do not contact,
    // already spoken to today, skipped by name — and a window that strips one
    // KIND of reason is the narrower answer whenever both are true. Read the
    // other way round, a customer marked do-not-contact whose only reason was
    // an order ask is explained to the telecaller as an order cooldown, and
    // the standing instruction never appears anywhere.
    //
    // Only the sentence moves. A customer held by either is held by both, so
    // nobody enters or leaves the list because of this.
    const held = suppressionReason(c, today, config, hasReminderReason, nowMs);

    if (!reasons.length) {
      // Nothing left but a reason one of the four windows says not yet. Shown
      // rather than dropped: a customer late by their own cycle would
      // otherwise vanish with no explanation.
      //
      // The order names the one that actually did the stripping. `quiet` and
      // `hold` both need an order or a promise, neither of which a suspect on
      // a ladder has, so a lead emptied by the funnel falls through to it.
      // `outcome` sits above the funnel because it is the more specific
      // answer where both apply — "they told us no on Tuesday" is what a
      // telecaller needs, and the funnel sentence is true of that lead every
      // day either way.
      //
      // The assertion holds because reasons only empties if a filter ran, and
      // a filter only runs if its own window is non-null.
      suppressed.push({
        customerId: c.customerId,
        name: c.name,
        reason: held ?? quiet ?? hold ?? outcome ?? funnel!,
      });
      continue;
    }

    if (held) {
      suppressed.push({ customerId: c.customerId, name: c.name, reason: held });
      continue;
    }

    reasons.sort((a, b) => b.weight - a.weight);
    entries.push({
      customerId: c.customerId,
      name: c.name,
      score: reasons[0].weight,
      reasons,
      outstanding: c.outstanding,
      // The leading reason decides which question "what is this worth" is
      // asking, so it is read after the sort, never before it.
      callValue: callValuePaise(reasons[0].kind, c),
      targetGap: c.targetGap,
      daysSinceContact: c.lastContactDate
        ? daysBetween(c.lastContactDate, today)
        : null,
    });
  }

  entries.sort(compareEntries);

  const limit = config["queue.maxSizePerUser"];
  return {
    entries: limit > 0 ? entries.slice(0, limit) : entries,
    suppressed,
    totalQualified: entries.length,
  };
}

export type QueueReasonKind =
  /** Money overdue and the collections engine says a call is due today. */
  | "paymentOverdue"
  | "reminderOverdue"
  | "reminderDueToday"
  | "orderOverdueFullCycle"
  /** Past the multiple of their own cycle that earns the Inactive badge. */
  | "orderLongOverdue"
  | "orderDue"
  /** The routine stock check, at a percentage of the customer's own cycle. */
  | "routineCall"
  | "prospect"
  | "checkInOverdue"
  | "checkInDue"
  /** An order already placed and still working its way through. */
  | "orderStatus"
  /** Rang, nobody answered, and the ladder says try again now. */
  | "noAnswerRetry"
  /** The ladder is exhausted; somebody has to decide what happens next. */
  | "unreachable";

export const DEFAULT_TIER_WEIGHTS: Record<QueueReasonKind, number> = {
  /* P1 — money, and promises made to a customer. */
  paymentOverdue: 110,
  reminderOverdue: 100,
  reminderDueToday: 90,
  /* P2 — the order that should have happened by now. */
  orderOverdueFullCycle: 80,
  orderDue: 70,
  /* P3 — routine work. */
  routineCall: 60,
  prospect: 55,
  checkInOverdue: 50,
  /*
   * P3.5 — the customer who stopped.
   *
   * Past the same multiple of their own cycle that earns the Inactive badge,
   * and deliberately BELOW every call about an order that is merely due. This
   * is the "why did you stop" conversation, which is worth having and is not
   * worth having first: there are 322 of these against 198 active customers,
   * and at `orderOverdueFullCycle`'s weight they filled every 60-row list and
   * pushed the people about to reorder off the bottom of it. Ranked here, they
   * are worked when the day's real chasing is done.
   */
  orderLongOverdue: 45,
  checkInDue: 40,
  /* P4 — chasing a ring nobody answered, and the state after it. */
  unreachable: 35,
  noAnswerRetry: 30,
  /* Not a call for an order at all: an order already on its way. */
  orderStatus: 10,
};

function weightOf(weights: Partial<Record<QueueReasonKind, number>>, kind: QueueReasonKind): number {
  return weights[kind] ?? DEFAULT_TIER_WEIGHTS[kind];
}

function compareEntries(a: QueueEntry, b: QueueEntry): number {
  if (b.score !== a.score) return b.score - a.score;
  if (b.callValue !== a.callValue) return b.callValue - a.callValue;
  if (b.outstanding !== a.outstanding) return b.outstanding - a.outstanding;
  if (b.targetGap !== a.targetGap) return b.targetGap - a.targetGap;
  const aContact = a.daysSinceContact ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
  const bContact = b.daysSinceContact ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
  if (bContact !== aContact) return bContact - aContact;
  return a.customerId.localeCompare(b.customerId); // stable
}

export function callValuePaise(
  topReason: QueueReasonKind,
  c: Pick<QueueCandidate, "outstanding" | "typicalOrderPaise" | "cycleConfidence">,
): number {
  if (topReason === "paymentOverdue") return c.outstanding;
  if (!isPrediction(topReason)) return c.typicalOrderPaise;
  /*
   * No confidence figure means NO DISCOUNT, not a middling one.
   *
   * A prediction takes a measured cycle and a measured cycle computes a
   * confidence, so in a database whose caches are current this is never null.
   * It is null on every cycle computed before the column existed — 297 of
   * them here — and those rebuild on the next nightly.
   *
   * Until they do, discounting them all by half would be a uniform penalty
   * dressed up as a judgement: it says "we are unsure about this customer"
   * when what is true is "we have not looked yet". Missing information never
   * demotes anybody; the discount starts applying to a customer the moment
   * there is something real to apply.
   */
  const sure = c.cycleConfidence ?? 100;
  return Math.round((c.typicalOrderPaise * sure) / 100);
}

export function routineDayFor(
  cycleDays: number,
  confidence: number | null,
  config: RoutineCallConfig,
): number {
  /*
   * A customer who buys every fortnight or less gets NO stock-check call, and
   * this is the ONLY thing a short cycle costs them. Their order is chased on
   * their own due date exactly like everybody else's — the quiet window is
   * capped at their cycle so that it cannot run past it.
   *
   * What they lose is the call BEFORE the order is due, which asks what they
   * have left on the shelf. Somebody buying every week already knows, and is in
   * contact constantly through the orders themselves, so it is noise on both
   * sides of the phone.
   *
   * Returning the cycle itself is what withholds it: the first day an order
   * reason can fire becomes the due date, never earlier.
   */
  if (cycleDays <= config["queue.routineMinCycleDays"]) return cycleDays;

  /*
   * Otherwise the stock check lands at a percentage of the customer's OWN
   * cycle — 70% of 30 days is day 21, three weeks after the last order and
   * nine days before the next is expected.
   *
   * Forwards from the last order, not backwards from the due date. The old
   * calculation subtracted a lead capped at ten days, which on a 60-day
   * customer meant day 50 rather than day 42: the longer the cycle, the later
   * the warning, which is backwards. A long cycle is exactly where the
   * estimate is loosest and the notice should be longest.
   */
  /*
   * ...and it moves with how predictable that cycle is.
   *
   * A date computed from 29, 30, 31 days is worth calling ON. A date computed
   * from 15, 45, 22, 60 is a guess dressed up as a date, and the honest
   * response to a guess is a wider net — ring earlier, because the real
   * order could come at any point either side of it.
   *
   * So a perfectly regular customer is called LATER, closer to the day they
   * actually order, which is the call least likely to be wasted; an erratic
   * one is called earlier. Fifty is neutral and leaves the flat percentage
   * exactly where it was, so a swing of zero restores the old behaviour for
   * everybody.
   */
  const swing = config["queue.routineConfidenceSwing"];
  const adjust = ((confidence ?? 50) - 50) / 50;
  const percent = clampPercent(
    config["queue.routineCallPercent"] + adjust * swing,
  );

  return Math.max(1, Math.round((cycleDays * percent) / 100));
}

function quietWindow(
  c: QueueCandidate,
  today: BusinessDate,
  config: QueueConfig,
  hasReminderReason: boolean,
): string | null {
  if (!c.lastOrderDate || hasReminderReason) return null;
  const quiet = quietDaysFor(c, config);
  const sinceOrder = daysBetween(c.lastOrderDate, today);
  if (sinceOrder >= quiet) return null;
  const left = quiet - sinceOrder;
  // The cycle is safe to name here. This sentence is only ever SHOWN when the
  // stripping above emptied the reason list, which takes an order reason, which
  // takes a measured cycle — so `cycleDays` is never the guessed default by the
  // time a telecaller reads it.
  return `Orders every ${c.cycleDays} days · ordered ${sinceOrder === 0 ? "today" : `${sinceOrder} day${sinceOrder === 1 ? "" : "s"} ago`} - no order chased for ${left} more day${left === 1 ? "" : "s"}`;
}

src/lib/engines/queue.ts#quietDaysFor.html:
function quietDaysFor(c: QueueCandidate, config: QueueConfig): number {
  const quiet = config["queue.quietDaysAfterOrder"];
  if (c.cycleIsDefault) return quiet;
  return Math.min(quiet, c.cycleDays);
}

function suppressionReason(
  c: QueueCandidate,
  today: BusinessDate,
  config: QueueConfig,
  hasReminderReason: boolean,
  nowMs: number,
): string | null {
  if (c.doNotContact) return "Marked do not contact";

  if (c.skippedTodayReason) return `Skipped today - ${c.skippedTodayReason}`;

  if (config["queue.excludeCalledToday"] && c.calledToday) {
    return "Already called today";
  }

  if (config["queue.excludeActiveInOrderSystem"] && c.activeInOrderSystem) {
    return "Active in the order system";
  }

  /*
   * Waiting for the next rung of the no-answer ladder. Held rather than
   * dropped, so somebody looking for a customer they rang this morning can
   * see when the next attempt is owed instead of concluding they vanished.
   */
  if (noAnswerState(c, today, config, nowMs) === "waiting") {
    return `No answer - attempt ${c.noAnswerCount} made, waiting before the next`;
  }

  // Only a CONFIRMED send suppresses. A copied-but-unconfirmed message means
  // the system does not know it was sent, and suppressing on that would drop
  // customers out of the calling list on the strength of something that may
  // never have happened.
  //
  // A reminder outranks this for the same reason it outranks the quiet window:
  // the callback was promised to the customer, and a message we chose to send
  // afterwards must not be what cancels it. Being called the day after a
  // WhatsApp is a small cost; not ringing somebody who asked to be rung is the
  // failure the cooldown was never meant to cause. `calledToday` still wins —
  // they have already been spoken to.
  if (c.lastConfirmedWhatsappDate && !hasReminderReason) {
    const cooldown = config["queue.whatsappCooldownDays"];
    const elapsed = daysBetween(c.lastConfirmedWhatsappDate, today);
    if (elapsed < cooldown) {
      const left = cooldown - elapsed;
      return `WhatsApp sent ${elapsed === 0 ? "today" : `${elapsed} day${elapsed === 1 ? "" : "s"} ago`} - ${left} day${left === 1 ? "" : "s"} of cooldown left`;
    }
  }

  return null;
}

src/lib/engines/queue.ts#isOrderChasing.html:
function isOrderChasing(kind: QueueReasonKind): boolean {
  return (
    kind === "orderDue" ||
    kind === "routineCall" ||
    kind === "orderOverdueFullCycle" ||
    kind === "orderStatus"
  );
}

src/lib/engines/queue.ts#isOrderAsk.html:
function isOrderAsk(kind: QueueReasonKind): boolean {
  return (
    isOrderChasing(kind) || kind === "prospect" || kind === "orderLongOverdue"
  );
}

src/lib/engines/queue.ts#isHoldableReaso.html:
function isHoldableReason(kind: QueueReasonKind): boolean {
  return (
    isOrderChasing(kind) ||
    kind === "checkInDue" ||
    kind === "checkInOverdue" ||
    kind === "prospect"
  );
}

export function noAnswerState(
  c: Pick<QueueCandidate, "noAnswerCount" | "lastNoAnswerAt">,
  today: BusinessDate,
  config: QueueConfig,
  nowMs: number,
): "none" | "waiting" | "due" | "exhausted" {
  if (!c.lastNoAnswerAt || c.noAnswerCount < 1) return "none";
  if (c.noAnswerCount >= config["queue.noAnswerMaxAttempts"]) return "exhausted";

  const lastMs = Date.parse(c.lastNoAnswerAt);
  if (Number.isNaN(lastMs)) return "none";

  if (c.noAnswerCount === 1) {
    const gapMs = config["queue.noAnswerRetryHours"] * 3_600_000;
    return nowMs - lastMs >= gapMs ? "due" : "waiting";
  }

  // Rung 2 onwards, in days: [1, 3] means the next working day, then three
  // days after that. Past the end of the ladder the last rung repeats until
  // the attempt limit stops it.
  const ladder = config["queue.noAnswerRetryDays"];
  const step = ladder[Math.min(c.noAnswerCount - 2, ladder.length - 1)] ?? 1;
  const lastDay = c.lastNoAnswerAt.slice(0, 10);
  return daysBetween(lastDay, today) >= step ? "due" : "waiting";
}

async function settleDayList(
  userId: string,
  day: BusinessDate,
  live: QueueResult,
  candidates: QueueCandidate[],
  config: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof getConfig>>,
): Promise<QueueResult> {
  const stored = await db
    .select()
    .from(queueSnapshots)
    .where(and(eq(queueSnapshots.day, day), eq(queueSnapshots.userId, userId)))
    .orderBy(asc(queueSnapshots.rank));

  if (!stored.length) {
    // First read of the business day. Write what the engine just decided.
    if (live.entries.length) {
      await db
        .insert(queueSnapshots)
        .values(
          live.entries.map((e, i) => ({
            day,
            userId,
            customerId: e.customerId,
            score: e.score,
            reasons: e.reasons,
            rank: i,
          })),
        )
        // Two tabs opening at once is one list, not a crash.
        .onConflictDoNothing();
    }
    return live;
  }

  /*
   * The day is already settled. Rebuild its entries from the stored rows, in
   * the stored order, and let today's live state decide what is still callable.
   */
  const liveById = new Map(live.entries.map((e) => [e.customerId, e]));
  const heldById = new Map(live.suppressed.map((h) => [h.customerId, h]));
  const byId = new Map(candidates.map((c) => [c.customerId, c]));

  const entries: QueueResult["entries"] = [];
  const suppressed = [...live.suppressed.filter((h) => !liveById.has(h.customerId))];

  for (const row of stored) {
    const candidate = byId.get(row.customerId);
    // Out of the book entirely since the list was settled — reassigned, or
    // deactivated. Not held back: it is not this person's to explain.
    if (!candidate) continue;

    const stillLive = liveById.get(row.customerId);
    if (stillLive) {
      // Keep the settled reason and rank; a customer does not get re-ranked
      // mid-morning because their outstanding moved.
      entries.push({
        customerId: row.customerId,
        name: candidate.name,
        score: row.score,
        reasons: (row.reasons.length
          ? row.reasons
          : stillLive.reasons) as QueueResult["entries"][number]["reasons"],
        outstanding: candidate.outstanding,
        // Recomputed from the settled reason against today's figures. The
        // RANK is frozen — a customer is not re-ranked mid-morning because
        // their outstanding moved — so this only ever describes the row; it
        // does not move it.
        callValue: callValuePaise(
          (row.reasons[0]?.kind ?? stillLive.reasons[0].kind) as Parameters<
            typeof callValuePaise
          >[0],
          candidate,
        ),
        targetGap: candidate.targetGap,
        daysSinceContact: stillLive.daysSinceContact,
      });
      continue;
    }

    // No longer callable. Say why, rather than letting it vanish.
    const held = heldById.get(row.customerId);
    if (!suppressed.some((h) => h.customerId === row.customerId)) {
      suppressed.push({
        customerId: row.customerId,
        name: candidate.name,
        reason: held?.reason ?? "Dealt with since the list was settled",
      });
    }
  }

  /*
   * A promise falling due today reopens the settled list — and only that.
   * Anything else waits for tomorrow, which is the point of settling it.
   */
  const settledIds = new Set(stored.map((r) => r.customerId));
  const promises = live.entries.filter(
    (e) =>
      !settledIds.has(e.customerId) &&
      e.reasons.some(
        (r) => r.kind === "reminderDueToday" || r.kind === "reminderOverdue",
      ),
  );
  if (promises.length) {
    entries.unshift(...promises);
    await db
      .insert(queueSnapshots)
      .values(
        promises.map((e, i) => ({
          day,
          userId,
          customerId: e.customerId,
          score: e.score,
          reasons: e.reasons,
          rank: -1 - i,
        })),
      )
      .onConflictDoNothing();
  }

  const limit = config["queue.maxSizePerUser"];
  return {
    entries: limit > 0 ? entries.slice(0, limit) : entries,
    suppressed,
    totalQualified: entries.length,
  };
}

export async function nextStepForCustomer(
  customerId: string,
): Promise<NextStep | null> {
  const ctx = await resolveScope();
  const day = await today();
  const { config, candidates } = await queueInputs([ctx.user.id], day, customerId);

  const candidate = candidates[0];
  if (!candidate) return null;

  // The collections engine's own conclusion, folded in exactly as the queue
  // folds it in — the verdict for today, and the date behind it so the search
  // can roll forward.
  let paymentNextCallOn: string | null = null;
  if (config["queue.includePaymentDue"]) {
    const cadence = await paymentCadenceFor(customerId);
    if (cadence) {
      paymentNextCallOn = cadence.nextCallOn;
      if (cadence.nextCallOn <= day) {
        candidate.paymentCallDue = {
          totalOverdue: cadence.totalOverdue,
          daysOverdue: cadence.daysOverdue,
        };
      }
    }
  }

  return nextStep({ candidate, paymentNextCallOn }, day, config, Date.now());
}

export function nextStep(
  input: NextStepInput,
  today: BusinessDate,
  config: QueueConfig,
  nowMs: number,
  horizonDays: number = NEXT_STEP_HORIZON_DAYS,
): NextStep {
  const { candidate, paymentNextCallOn } = input;

  /*
   * Why they are not on the list today, in the words the held-back strip
   * already uses. Taken before the search so the two sentences agree.
   *
   * The call just logged is discounted on purpose. "Already called today" is
   * the first reason the queue reaches for and it is the one thing the person
   * reading this does not need telling — they made the call. What they want is
   * the rule underneath: the five days a "no order" buys, the quiet after an
   * order, the WhatsApp cooldown. Where that is genuinely all there is, the
   * plain answer is used.
   */
  const asIfNotCalled = { ...candidate, calledToday: false };
  const underneath = buildQueue(
    [forDay(asIfNotCalled, today, today, paymentNextCallOn)],
    today,
    config,
    nowMs,
  ).suppressed[0]?.reason;
  const plain = buildQueue(
    [forDay(candidate, today, today, paymentNextCallOn)],
    today,
    config,
    nowMs,
  ).suppressed[0]?.reason;
  const heldToday = underneath ?? plain ?? null;

  for (let i = 0; i <= horizonDays; i++) {
    const day = addDays(today, i);
    const c = forDay(candidate, day, today, paymentNextCallOn);
    const result =
      i === 0
        ? buildQueue([c], day, config, nowMs)
        : buildQueue([c], day, config);

    const entry = result.entries[0];
    if (!entry) continue;

    const top = entry.reasons[0];
    return withPromise(
      describe(top.kind, top.label, day, today, i, heldToday),
      candidate,
      today,
    );
  }

  if (candidate.doNotContact) {
    return {
      kind: "none",
      date: null,
      daysAway: null,
      reasonKind: null,
      headline: "No next call",
      detail:
        "This customer is marked do not contact, so nothing will bring them back to your Call Log.",
      heldToday: null,
      promise: null,
    };
  }

  return {
    kind: "none",
    date: null,
    daysAway: null,
    reasonKind: null,
    headline: "Nothing scheduled",
    detail: `Nothing brings this customer back to your Call Log in the next ${horizonDays} days. They will appear when something changes — an order falls due, or somebody sets a reminder.`,
    heldToday,
    promise: null,
  };
}

search.text: The Call Log is a pure engine ( buildQueue ) fed by one service ( queue-service.ts ) and settled once a day into queue snapshots . The screen renders what the service returns; saving a call goes through saveInteraction , which ends by computing and storing the next-step sentence on the call. Every code block below is cut from the source this deployment was built from.

search.text: The whole pipeline: reasons → unreachable short-circuit → four windows → whole-customer suppression → rank → cap.

search.heading: The reasons and their weights
search.text: A stored queue.tierWeights replaces the default object wholesale, so weightOf falls back per kind — a blob written before a kind existed would otherwise give it undefined , and undefined arithmetic does not throw, it silently poisons the sort.

search.heading: Ordering
search.text: typicalOrderPaise is a cache on customers.typical order paise , written by writeCycle in lib/recompute.ts from approved orders over queue.orderValueLookbackDays . Fix a wrong value by re-running the recompute, never by updating the row.

search.text: routineDayFor is also read by the lead-nurture engine for the repeat-order call — change it and both move.

search.heading: Windows and suppression
search.text: The four windows strip reason kinds ; suppressionReason holds the whole customer . It is read before the "emptied by a window" sentence on purpose: a do-not-contact customer whose only reason was an order ask must be explained as do-not-contact, not as a cooldown. search.heading: The no-answer ladder
search.text: The count is consecutiveNoAnswerSql in queue-service.ts : outbound no answer calls since the latest call with any other non-null outcome.

search.heading: Saving a call
search.text: saveInteraction ( lib/services/interaction-service.ts ) validates outside the transaction, then writes everything in one transaction : the order ( pending approval ), reminders from the outcome and next actions, the complaint, the calls row, opportunities, timeline events, product lines, and the customer's last call date / last contact date / last order date / do not contact . Recomputes (buying cycle, inactivity, outstanding, follow-up state) run after commit. An idempotency key that already exists returns the stored next step and Already logged — a double-click cannot show a second answer.

search.heading: The next step is stored, not cached
search.text: Never let a recompute touch these. lib/recompute.ts must not learn to rebuild the next step columns. A cache answers "when is the next call" and is rebuilt when the answer changes; these answer "what did we tell the person who logged this call, on that day", and rebuilding them destroys the question. Same kind of mark as orders.approved at .

search.heading: Changing the Call Log safely
search.text: Put the rule in the engine, and only there. A new reason, window or suppression belongs in engines/queue.ts . next-step.ts re-asks buildQueue , so the "comes back on" sentence follows automatically — never re-derive a rule in a second place. Make every threshold a setting. Add the key to registry.ts (with a Config type entry), read it through QueueConfig . No number a manager might change is a constant. Suppress, never drop. Anything that keeps a customer off the list must return a sentence for the held-back strip. Give a new reason kind everything it needs. A weight in DEFAULT TIER WEIGHTS , a tone in REASON TONE (queue-screen), a short name in REASON BADGE (call panel), wording in describe() (next-step), and a filter pill if it is one. Test it in engines.test.ts first. The engine is pure; a rule without a test is a rule nobody can tell has broken.

The Call Log is your day's work. Every morning it lists the customers you should ring, in the order you should ring them , and every name carries the reason it is there. You work it top to bottom: call, log what happened, move to the next row. The numbers on this page — how many days, how many attempts — are the settings your CRM is using right now, read live. If a manager changes one on the Settings screen, this page changes with it.

search.heading: The screen at a glance
search.text: The Call Log, for a telecaller working their own book. Call Log Re-prioritise Call Customer A 12 of 48 worked 25% Connected today. 9 Connect rate. 75% Missed. 3 Orders today. 4 Booked today. ₹1.8L To work 36 Reminder due 4 No answer 6 Due to reorder 17 Check-in due 5 Leads 3 Inactive 2 j / k to move · Enter to open the call panel 7 customers held back today — nothing disappears silently

search.heading: Your day, step by step
search.text: Open the Call Log. The list is put together the first time anybody opens it each morning and then stays settled for the day — the order does not reshuffle under you while you work. The only thing that can jump in during the day is a reminder falling due: a callback you promised is added at the top. Start at the top row. The first row is your next call. Press Call (or Enter ) to open the call panel. The panel shows who they are, what they buy, what they owe, their last three calls — and the reason you are ringing. Make the call, then log what happened. Choose how the interaction happened, then the outcome, then fill in what the outcome asks for. Details are in Logging a call below. Read what happens next, then move on. After saving, a small window tells you when this customer comes back to your Call Log and why . Press Next customer — or use Save & next ▸ in the panel to save and move in one go. When the list is empty. You will see Queue cleared for today . The suggested next work is the Payment Follow-up list.

search.heading: Reading a row: what each reason means
search.text: Every customer is on the list for at least one reason. The colour tells you how urgent it is: red is overdue, amber is due today or needs attention, purple is routine sales work, grey is lower priority. Reason on the row Short name in the panel What it means What to do Payment overdue N days – ₹X Payment overdue Collections wants a call now. Only shown when payments are switched on for the Call Log (currently ). Chase the payment. Reminder N days overdue – note Reminder overdue A callback somebody promised is late. Ring them — they are expecting it. Reminder due today – note Reminder due today A promised callback is today. Ring them today. Order overdue by N full cycles Order overdue They have missed at least one whole order cycle. Ask for the order. Order overdue by N days / Order due today Order due Their order is due by their own buying pattern. Ask for the order. Stock check – orders every N days Stock check They are partway through their cycle. A good time to ask what is left on the shelf. Ask about stock, take the order if there is one. Never ordered – N days since last contact Never ordered A lead that has not bought yet. Try for a first order. No contact for N days – cycle not established yet Check-in overdue A customer whose buying pattern is not known yet, and it has been a while. Check in. Gone quiet – N cycles since their last order Stopped ordering They used to buy and have stopped. Ranked below orders that are merely due, on purpose. Ask why they stopped. Check-in due – N days since last contact Check-in due Routine check-in for a customer whose pattern is not known yet. Check in. Unreachable – N attempts, no answer Cannot reach them Rung several times in a row with no answer. Decide what happens next — a different number, a visit, or leave them. No answer – attempt N No answer – try again A retry after an earlier unanswered call. Ring again. Order in progress – status Order in progress An order is waiting for accounts or dispatch. Check on their order if they ask. The row also shows the contact person, phone, last order date, how long since anybody spoke to them, and the last note anybody wrote. Read the last note before you dial.

search.heading: Logging a call
search.text: The call panel, logging an outbound call that ended in an order. Customer A · contact person · phone. Reminder overdue Stock check We Called Them They Called Us Order Received Order Taken No Order No Answer Payment Promised Follow-up … 2 products · 14 cans · 152 L Confirm dispatch Send price list Save log Save & next ▸

search.heading: What each outcome asks you for
search.text: Outcome You must fill in What it does Order Taken Products and quantities Creates an order waiting for accounts to approve. No Order Why there was no order (one choice) They will not be asked for an order again for a few days — see Why is somebody missing below. No Answer Why (no response, busy, switched off…) Starts the retry ladder. The panel tells you which attempt this is. Payment Promised — Creates a payment-promise reminder, days out unless you set another date. Follow-up What you are waiting for Creates a reminder, day out unless you set another date. Complaint What they are asking for, category, description; photographs optional Raises a complaint (or adds to an open one of the same kind). Not Interested Why; whether there is a "later"; a date if there is "They asked us not to call again" marks the customer do not contact . Casual Talk Purpose Records the contact. Transport Follow-up — Records a delivery chase. For a call they made, you also choose who called (owner, purchase, accounts…) and why — answer those before the outcome. A common mistake. Logging an order that came in on WhatsApp as We Called Them → Order Taken . Use Order Received instead and give the order date — otherwise the record says you rang them on a day you did not.

search.heading: After you save: when they come back
search.text: The window that opens after a save tells you, in one fixed sentence, when this customer comes back to your Call Log : Comes back to your Call Log on Mon 1 Sep — 13 days away Ask for the order — they are due to reorder. The badge beside it tells you what kind of date that is: Promised. A callback the customer asked for. You owe them this call on that day. Scheduled. The date the rules give today. It moves if they order, pay or ask for a callback before then. Needs a decision. Nobody can reach them. There is no next call until somebody decides what to do. Nothing scheduled. Marked do not contact, or nothing brings them back within four months. If you have just promised a callback, the window offers Hold other calls until date . Press it to stop the Call Log asking you about orders or check-ins for this customer until the day you promised — money and reminders are never held.

search.heading: Customers held back today
search.text: The held-back strip, opened. 7 customers held back today. Nobody disappears from the Call Log without a reason. If you expected somebody and they are not there, open the held-back strip — the sentence beside their name is the rule that kept them off today. The How it works tab explains each rule.

search.heading: When nobody answers
search.text: You do not need to remember when to try again. The Call Log brings them back: The no-answer ladder. Any answered call puts them back to normal.. The same-day wait is hour(s). After unanswered calls in a row the customer is marked Unreachable and the row asks you to decide what happens next instead of ringing again.

search.heading: Skipping and closing an account
search.text: From the row menu (⋯): - Skip for today — takes them off today's list. You must say why; the reason is recorded and shown in the held-back strip. They come back tomorrow if they are still due. - Request deactivation — asks a manager to close the account (shop shut, duplicate, not a customer). The manager decides on the Close / Reopen screen. Until then the row says Deactivation already requested . - Send WhatsApp instead and See their bills open those screens for this customer.

search.heading: Keyboard shortcuts
search.text: Key Does j Move down the list k Move up the list Enter Open the call panel on the selected row Inside the panel, ◀ Previous and Next ▶ walk the list in the order it is shown.

search.heading: For managers: the team view
search.text: A manager sees the whole team's Call Log by default, with an extra Assigned to column saying whose call each row is (or Unassigned , which is the one to look at first). Switch to My book in the header to see only your own. A telecaller always sees only their own book.

search.heading: Why is somebody (not) on my list?
search.text: A customer I expected is not on the list and not in the held-back strip either.. They have no reason to be called today: not yet at their stock-check day, a lead contacted within the last days, or nothing due. Nothing is wrong — their day has not come. It says 'Already called today'.. Somebody — you or a colleague — logged a call with them today. Even a due reminder does not bring them back the same day. They ordered four days ago. Why no stock check?. After an order there is a quiet period of up to days (shorter for customers who order more often than that). Somebody who just ordered is serving themselves. A reminder you set still comes through. I told them 'no order' two days ago and they are not on the list.. A No Order answer buys a few days before the Call Log asks them for an order again. Only the order question is held — a reminder, a payment or a check-in still shows. It says 'WhatsApp sent … cooldown left'.. A WhatsApp message to them was confirmed sent in the last days. A message you copied but did not confirm does not count. A due reminder overrides this. It says 'Active in the order system'.. They have an order still open on the order sheet's Taken Order tab. Calling them for another order would be asking twice. It says 'On the sales team's lead funnel'.. The field sales team is working this lead towards an order, so the Call Log does not ask for one as well. Somebody owes a lot of money but is not on my Call Log.. Payment chasing lives on the Payment Follow-up screen. It only appears on the Call Log when a manager switches that on (currently ). The list is shorter than I expected.. The Call Log shows at most customers a day. The progress count includes everyone who qualified. It says 'Dealt with since the list was settled'.. They were on this morning's list but no longer need a call — for example they ordered, or somebody already rang them.

The Call Log answers one question every morning: of everybody in this book, who should be rung today, and in what order? It is not a contact schedule. It chases orders — each customer is called from their own buying pattern, and everything else (reminders, leads, check-ins, money) is fitted around that. This tab explains every rule that decides the list, why it is that rule, and the setting that changes it. Every value quoted is the one your CRM is using right now; amber means a manager has changed it from the shipped default.

search.heading: How a customer gets onto the list
search.text: From the whole book to today's list. Three things are deliberate about this shape: 1. Nobody vanishes silently. A customer the rules keep off the list goes into the held-back strip with a sentence saying why. A telecaller must always be able to find out why somebody they expected is missing. 2. Windows silence a kind of call, not the customer. A customer who ordered yesterday still appears if a reminder or a check-in is due — only the order chasing is removed. 3. The list is settled once a day. It is built on the first read of the morning and then kept, so the order does not reshuffle under somebody halfway down it.

search.heading: The reasons, and how they are ranked
search.text: Every customer on the list has at least one reason . The strongest reason decides where they sit. The ranking is a configurable weight per reason: Money and promises first, then orders that should already have happened, then routine work. A callback the customer asked for is a promise; not making it is worse than any order missed. "Stopped ordering" deliberately sits below every order that is merely due: the "why did you stop" conversation is worth having, but at one time there were more lapsed customers than active ones, and ranked higher they pushed the people about to reorder off the bottom of the list.

search.heading: Within the same reason: what the call is worth
search.text: Two customers both "due to order" are not equal. Within a reason, the list is ordered by what the call is worth : - A payment call is worth the amount owed. - An order call is worth the customer's typical order — the median of their own approved orders over the last days. Never a figure from the catalogue: the product master has no prices. - A prediction (order due, stock check, overdue, stopped) is discounted by how sure we are of the customer's pattern . Somebody who orders every 29, 30, 31 days is a safer bet than somebody who orders after 15, 45, 22 and 60. A customer whose confidence has never been measured is not discounted. Missing information must never demote anybody. After value, ties are broken by: outstanding balance, gap to target, longest since anybody spoke to them.

search.heading: Calling from the customer's own buying cycle
search.text: Every customer with enough history has a buying cycle — the typical number of days between their orders — and a confidence in it. The Call Log uses the cycle to decide every order-related reason. The stock check: before the order is due. For a customer with a measured cycle, the Call Log rings partway through the cycle to ask what is left on the shelf. The day is % of the cycle, moved by up to points by confidence: a very regular customer is called later , closer to the day they really order; an erratic one earlier , because the honest answer to a guess is a wider net. Customers whose cycle is days or shorter get no stock check — somebody buying every week already knows their shelf. Their order is chased on its due date like everyone else's. A 30-day customer Confidence unknown or 50% Very regular (100%) Erratic (0%) Stock check from day 21 24 18 Worked with the shipped settings (70%, swing 10). Due, overdue, and stopped. - Order due — the day their cycle says they should order, and until they have missed a whole cycle. - Order overdue by a full cycle — at least one whole cycle missed. - Stopped ordering — they have gone × their own cycle without an order. The same multiple marks the customer Inactive on their record, so the Call Log and the customer list cannot disagree about who has lapsed. One customer with a 30-day cycle, across one cycle, with the shipped settings: Days since their last order What the Call Log does 1 – 15 Quiet no order chased — they have just bought 16 – 20 Nothing — no reason to ring yet 21 – 29 Stock check ask what is left on the shelf 30 Order due today 31 – 59 Order overdue 60 onwards Stopped ordering ask why they stopped Customers without a measured cycle. A customer needs enough orders before a cycle means anything. Until then they get a steady check-in : due after days without contact, overdue at one and a half times that. A guessed cycle never earns a stock-check or due date — chasing on a guess rings a quarterly buyer every month. Leads. A lead who has never ordered is called every days, counted from the last contact (or from when they were added, if nobody has spoken to them yet). Two kinds of lead are not prospected: a shop we deliver to through a distributor (a third-party customer ), and a lead the field team is working on the lead funnel.

search.heading: What holds a customer back
search.text: Some rules remove one kind of call and leave the rest. Others hold the whole customer back for the day.

search.heading: Windows: silence the order question, not the customer
search.text: Quiet after an order. No order is chased within days of the last one — or the customer's own cycle, if that is shorter and measured . Somebody who ordered days ago is serving themselves. The cap matters: a flat 15 days used to run past the due date of anybody ordering every week, so the customers ordering most often were chased last, and late. Now every customer follows one rule: quiet until their order is due, chased from the day it is. What the customer said last time. After an answered call, the order question rests for a time that depends on the answer: Without this, a customer past their call day returns to the top of the list every day until they order — which punishes the telecaller for working it. Only the ask is silenced; a reminder, a debt or a check-in still comes through. Held by a promised callback. When a telecaller promises a callback and presses Hold other calls until… , order and check-in calls for that customer stop until the promised day. Money, reminders and "unreachable" are never held. On the lead funnel. A lead the sales team is climbing the lead ladder with is not cold-called by the office and not chased for a reorder — otherwise two people chase one customer, neither knowing about the other. The lead still appears in the held-back strip with the reason.

search.heading: Held back for the whole day
search.text: These are checked in this order, and the first one that applies is the sentence shown: Order Held back because A due reminder overrides it? 1 Marked do not contact No — a standing instruction 2 Skipped today , with the reason given No 3 Already called today by anybody (setting: ) No — the contact has happened 4 Active in the order system — an open line on the Taken Order tab (setting: ) No — they have already ordered 5 Waiting before the next no-answer retry No 6 WhatsApp confirmed sent within days Yes Why a reminder beats the WhatsApp cooldown. The cooldown used to be the one rule that did not bend. A marketing message sent on Tuesday silently cancelled a call promised for Wednesday — a broken promise caused by something we chose to do. A reminder now overrides the quiet window, the "told us no" window and the WhatsApp cooldown. It does not override do-not-contact, a call already made today, or an open order: the first is an instruction and the others mean the contact has already happened. Copied is not sent. Only a WhatsApp message a person confirmed as sent starts the cooldown. A message copied and never confirmed is a customer who may or may not have heard from us, and it is shown as exactly that.

search.heading: When nobody answers
search.text: The no-answer ladder. - The second attempt comes after hour(s), the same day. - Later attempts wait days — one rung per attempt, the last rung repeating. - After unanswered calls in a row the customer becomes Unreachable : one row, one reason, and a question for a person rather than a sixth ring. - Any answered call resets the count.

search.heading: The list is settled once a day
search.text: The first time a telecaller's Call Log is read on a working day, the list is stored . Every later read that day keeps that order and those reasons. During the day: - A customer who no longer needs a call (they ordered, somebody rang them) leaves the list and appears in the held-back strip as Dealt with since the list was settled . - A reminder falling due is added at the top — a promise outranks a settled list. - The list never grows by any other route, so somebody halfway down it is never pushed back up by a reshuffle. The Call Log shows at most customers (0 means no limit). The progress count still counts everybody who qualified.

search.heading: What saving a call does
search.text: Saving a call is one transaction : the call, any order, reminder or complaint it produced, and the customer's rolled-up figures are written together or not at all. Half-saved calls are how telecaller data goes wrong. Saving a call. What the telecaller is told is kept, and never rewritten. The sentence shown after saving — Comes back to your Call Log on Mon 1 Sep — is stored on the call. It is a record of what the telecaller was told on that day, not a forecast that is kept up to date. If the customer orders the next morning, the customer's real next call changes; the old sentence does not, and the difference is the record of what changed. The Call History screen shows these stored answers. An order is the customer saying yes, not the business. An order taken on a call waits for accounts to approve it . "Did the customer order" is true at once, and stops the Call Log chasing them; "did we sell anything" is only true after approval, and is what targets, EOD value and the buying cycle count.

search.heading: Who sees whose list
search.text: - A telecaller sees only their own book. They cannot widen it. - A manager sees their team (their direct reports and themselves) by default, and can switch to their own book. An admin sees everyone. - Whose book a customer is in is one definition used by every list in the CRM: a lead belongs to its owner; a customer to its sales account manager. A team list says whose call each row is, and says Unassigned in words — a call nobody owns is the one a manager most needs to see.

search.heading: Every setting that shapes the Call Log
Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: These were found while writing this page. They are listed so nobody is surprised by them; each is a candidate for a fix. Settings on the screen that change nothing. Lead call percentage , lead minimum / maximum days and Quiet days after "no order" ( queue.leadPercent , queue.leadMinDays , queue.leadMaxDays , queue.noOrderCooldownDays ) are shown on the Settings screen but no longer read by the Call Log. The "no order" quiet now comes from How long each answer buys above. Hour the queue is snapshotted ( queue.snapshotHour ) only changes a sentence — the list is settled on the first read of the day, whatever the hour. - Unreachable customers skip the hold-back checks. A customer who has reached the no-answer limit is listed even if marked do-not-contact or already called today. - A pending no-answer retry hides a due reminder for the length of the wait. - Only calls we made start the "told us no" quiet. An inbound "No order" buys none. - The retry ladder counts calendar days , though the setting's description says working days. - Re-prioritise re-reads the settled list; it does not rebuild it. Only an administrator's rebuild does. - The morning warm-up job builds lists without payment calls, so on days it runs before anybody opens the Call Log, payment reasons are missing from the settled list even when payments are switched on.
